review: The hymn is Hebrews 12:2 with Isaiah 53:2–5: 1:1–8 is Lam 3:41 and Ps 25:1 with Phil 2:6–8, 2:1–8 is Isa 53:5 (מְחֹלָל מִפְּשָׁעֵנוּ) with Matt 27:29 (עֲטֶרֶת קוֹצִים), and 3:1–4 is Heb 12:2 (בּוֹזֶה לַבּוּשָׁה … יָשַׁב לִימִין כִּסֵּא הָאֱלֹהִים) almost verbatim.

2:5–8 הֲיֵשׁ עֲטֶרֶת … אַךְ־לוֹ עֲטֶרֶת חֶרְפָּה — the Arabic keeps a question and then a double negative (هَلْ لَهُ … تَاجٌ؟ لَا وَلَا سَيْفُ الظَّفَر), and the Hebrew keeps both moves: the question, the refusal, and then the ironic crown. The stanza's force is that the King's only crown is the one the soldiers braided.

2:3 רֹשֶׁם דְּקִירָה וּפְצָעִים — the Arabic إِثْرُ طَعْنٍ وَجِرَاحٍ is 'a trace of piercing and wounds'; רֹשֶׁם is post-biblical for an impress, used because the line needs the visible mark and the biblical verbs (רָשַׁם occurs only in Lev 26:35's sense of 'pay off') do not supply the noun.

3:1–2 הוּא נָשָׂא אֶת־הַצְּלָב / בּוֹזֶה לַבּוּשָׁה — the Hebrew follows Heb 12:2's order, cross then shame, whereas the Arabic puts the shame first; the verse is quoted, so the order is restored even though the Arabic's rhetoric ran the other way.

3:7 וְנַעֲמֹד לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד — the Arabic وَنَظَلُّ لِلدُّهُورِ is 'we abide for the ages'; עָמַד is the biblical verb for standing in God's presence (Ps 24:3, מִי־יָקוּם בִּמְקוֹם קָדְשׁוֹ), so the line is about continuance before Him and not merely duration.
